hinweis: Profiles summarized in our own words, measurements rounded. Conservation status follows the IUCN Red List and may differ today. The facts were written from general knowledge and are not checked against a source.

loewe.wo: Africa south of the Sahara, small population in India
loewe.m: up to 2.1 m long, up to 225 kg
loewe.f: The only big cat that lives in prides. Its roar can be heard up to 8 km away.

elefant.m: up to 3.3 m shoulder height, up to 6,000 kg
elefant.e: Grass, leaves, bark, up to 150 kg a day
elefant.f: The largest land animal on Earth. Elephants also communicate with deep sounds that humans cannot hear.

giraffe.m: up to 5.5 m tall, up to 1,900 kg
giraffe.f: The tallest animal on Earth. Despite its length, the neck has only 7 vertebrae, just like in humans.

zebra.m: up to 1.4 m shoulder height, up to 380 kg
zebra.f: Every zebra has its own stripe pattern, like a fingerprint.

gnu.m: up to 1.45 m shoulder height, up to 270 kg
gnu.f: Over 1 million wildebeest travel in a circle through the Serengeti and Masai Mara every year, following the rain.

antilope.m: up to 0.9 m shoulder height, up to 75 kg
antilope.f: Impalas jump up to 3 m high and 10 m far, often just to confuse hunters.

gazelle.m: up to 0.7 m shoulder height, up to 35 kg
gazelle.f: It reaches about 80 km/h and zigzags when fleeing, which a cheetah can hardly follow.

nashorn.m: up to 1.8 m shoulder height, up to 3,600 kg
nashorn.f: The horn is made of keratin, like our fingernails. Poaching is its biggest threat.

gepard.wo: Africa, very small population in Iran
gepard.m: up to 1.5 m long, up to 65 kg
gepard.f: The fastest land animal: about 100 km/h, but only for around 300 m.

leopard.m: up to 1.9 m long, up to 90 kg
leopard.f: It drags its prey up into trees so that lions and hyenas cannot get it.

hyaene.m: up to 1.6 m long, up to 80 kg
hyaene.e: Animals it hunts itself, and carrion
hyaene.f: It hunts very successfully itself and can crack even bones with its bite. The females lead the clan.

bueffel.m: up to 1.7 m shoulder height, up to 900 kg
bueffel.f: The herd defends itself together and even drives away lions.

warzenschwein.m: up to 0.85 m shoulder height, up to 150 kg
warzenschwein.f: It often eats on its knees and runs with its tail held straight up.

flusspferd.m: up to 1.6 m shoulder height, up to 3,200 kg
flusspferd.f: It stays in the water during the day and walks onto land at night to graze. It is one of the most dangerous animals in Africa.

okapi.m: up to 1.6 m shoulder height, up to 350 kg
okapi.f: The closest relative of the giraffe. Science described it only in 1901.

gorilla.m: up to 1.8 m upright, up to 200 kg
gorilla.f: Gorillas live in families led by a silverback. They share about 98 percent of their genes with us.

schimpanse.m: up to 1.7 m upright, up to 70 kg
schimpanse.f: Our closest relative. It uses tools, for example sticks to fish for termites.

pavian.m: up to 0.9 m long, up to 35 kg
pavian.e: Almost anything: grass, fruit, small animals
pavian.f: Baboons live in groups of up to 150 animals with a clear pecking order.

erdmaennchen.m: up to 0.35 m long, up to 1 kg
erdmaennchen.f: One of them always keeps watch and warns with its own calls, depending on whether the danger comes from the ground or from the air.

tiger.wo: South and Southeast Asia, Russian Far East
tiger.m: up to 3 m long, up to 300 kg
tiger.f: The largest cat in the world. Tigers like to swim, and the stripes can also be seen on the skin.

schneeleopard.m: up to 1.3 m long, up to 55 kg
schneeleopard.f: Its long tail helps with balance when climbing and works as a blanket when sleeping.

panda.m: up to 1.5 m long, up to 125 kg
panda.e: Almost only bamboo, up to 38 kg a day
panda.f: A bear that eats almost only bamboo. An extended bone works like a thumb and helps it grip.

orang.m: up to 1.4 m upright, up to 90 kg
orang.f: The largest animal that lives mostly in trees. Every night it builds itself a new sleeping nest.

makak.m: up to 0.65 m long, up to 12 kg
makak.f: It lives in the middle of Indian cities and many people there consider it sacred.

eisbaer.m: up to 2.6 m long, up to 700 kg
eisbaer.f: The largest land predator. The skin is black, the hairs are transparent and only look white.

rentier.m: up to 1.2 m shoulder height, up to 300 kg
rentier.f: The only deer species where the females also carry antlers.

moschusochse.wo: Canada, Greenland, small populations in Norway
moschusochse.m: up to 1.5 m shoulder height, up to 400 kg
moschusochse.f: When in danger, the herd forms a circle with the young in the middle.

polarfuchs.m: up to 0.7 m long, up to 8 kg
polarfuchs.f: White in winter, brown in summer. It does not freeze even at minus 50 degrees.

elch.m: up to 2.3 m shoulder height, up to 700 kg
elch.f: The largest deer species in the world. It swims well and dives up to 5 m deep for plants.

wolf.m: up to 1.6 m long, up to 70 kg
wolf.f: The ancestor of all dogs. A pack is usually simply a family.

baer.m: up to 2.8 m long, up to 600 kg
baer.f: In winter it rests for months without eating or drinking.

reh.m: up to 0.8 m shoulder height, up to 35 kg
reh.f: Not a child of the red deer, but a species of its own. Only the male carries antlers.

hirsch.m: up to 1.5 m shoulder height, up to 300 kg
hirsch.f: It sheds its antlers every year and grows them again. This is the fastest growing bone tissue of all mammals.

wildschwein.m: up to 1.1 m shoulder height, up to 200 kg
wildschwein.f: An omnivore with a fine nose. Thousands live in the middle of Berlin.

fuchs.m: up to 0.9 m long, up to 14 kg
fuchs.f: The most widespread predator in the world.

luchs.m: up to 1.3 m long, up to 35 kg
luchs.f: The largest cat in Europe, recognizable by the tufts of hair on its ears. It was reintroduced in the Harz.

dachs.m: up to 0.9 m long, up to 17 kg
dachs.f: Its burrow is passed down through generations and can be centuries old.

hase.m: up to 0.7 m long, up to 6 kg
hase.f: Young hares are born with open eyes and fur, unlike rabbits.

eichhoernchen.m: up to 0.25 m long, up to 0.4 kg
eichhoernchen.f: It buries supplies and does not find nearly all of them again. That is how it plants new trees.

igel.m: up to 0.3 m long, up to 1.5 kg
igel.f: About 6,000 spines protect it. In winter it lowers its body temperature almost to that of its surroundings.

waschbaer.m: up to 0.65 m long, up to 9 kg
waschbaer.f: Its hands feel almost as finely as ours. Especially many live in Kassel.

steinbock.m: up to 0.95 m shoulder height, up to 120 kg
steinbock.f: Almost wiped out, today there are around 50,000 animals again. It even climbs steep dam walls.

bison.m: up to 1.9 m shoulder height, up to 1,000 kg
bison.f: Once 30 million, around 1890 fewer than 1,000 animals. Today the largest land mammal in North America.

kojote.m: up to 1 m long, up to 20 kg
kojote.f: Today it lives in the middle of Los Angeles and New York.

puma.r: From the mountains to the jungle
puma.m: up to 1.9 m long, up to 100 kg
puma.f: The largest cat that does not roar. It purrs and hisses and jumps up to 5 m high.

jaguar.m: up to 1.8 m long, up to 150 kg
jaguar.f: Has the strongest bite of all big cats for its size. It cracks turtle shells.

tapir.m: up to 1.1 m shoulder height, up to 320 kg
tapir.f: Its short trunk grabs leaves. When diving, it works as a snorkel.

capybara.m: up to 1.3 m long, up to 65 kg
capybara.f: The largest rodent in the world. It can dive for up to 5 minutes.

kaenguru.m: up to 1.8 m upright, up to 90 kg
kaenguru.f: Jumps up to 9 m far and reaches over 50 km/h. The young grows up in the pouch.

koala.m: up to 0.85 m long, up to 14 kg
koala.f: Sleeps up to 20 hours a day because its toxic food provides hardly any energy. Not a bear, but a marsupial.

wombat.m: up to 1.2 m long, up to 40 kg
wombat.f: Its droppings are cube shaped. That way they do not roll away and mark its territory.

dingo.m: up to 1.2 m long, up to 20 kg
dingo.f: Came to Australia with humans about 4,000 years ago. It hardly barks, it howls.

wisent.m: up to 1.9 m shoulder height, up to 900 kg
wisent.f: The heaviest land animal in Europe. In 1927 it was extinct in the wild, and all bison today descend from only 12 zoo animals.

biber.m: up to 1 m long, up to 30 kg
biber.f: It builds dams and lodges and so changes whole landscapes. Its teeth grow for a lifetime.

otter.m: up to 1.3 m long including tail, up to 12 kg
otter.f: Its fur is among the densest of all animals and keeps it warm in the water.

murmeltier.r: Alpine pastures above the tree line
murmeltier.m: up to 0.6 m long, up to 8 kg
murmeltier.f: In danger it warns with a shrill whistle. It sleeps through about 6 months of winter in its burrow.

oryx.m: up to 1.2 m shoulder height, up to 240 kg
oryx.f: It can go a long time without drinking water. Its horns grow over 1 m long.

kudu.m: up to 1.6 m shoulder height, up to 315 kg
kudu.f: The twisted horns of the bull are among the longest of all antelopes.

ameisenbaer.m: up to 2 m long including tail, up to 40 kg
ameisenbaer.f: It has no teeth, but a tongue of about 60 cm. It eats up to 30,000 insects a day.

guerteltier.m: up to 0.8 m long including tail, up to 6 kg
guerteltier.f: It almost always gives birth to identical quadruplets.

faultier.m: up to 0.8 m long, up to 6 kg
faultier.f: It comes down from the tree only about once a week. Algae grow in its fur and camouflage it.

nasenbaer.m: up to 1.1 m long including tail, up to 7 kg
nasenbaer.f: It carries its long tail upright like an antenna and lives in groups of up to 30 animals.

lemur.m: up to 0.45 m long, tail up to 0.6 m, up to 3.5 kg
lemur.f: The females lead the group. In the morning, ring tailed lemurs sit in the sun with open arms.

schnabeltier.m: up to 0.6 m long, up to 2.4 kg
schnabeltier.f: A mammal that lays eggs. The males carry venomous spurs on their hind legs.

kamel.wo: North Africa, Arabia, India, feral in Australia
kamel.m: up to 2 m shoulder height, up to 600 kg
kamel.f: The hump holds fat, not water. It can go for weeks without drinking and then drink over 100 liters at once.

wasserbueffel.wo: Asia, today also Europe and South America
wasserbueffel.m: up to 1.9 m shoulder height, up to 1,200 kg
wasserbueffel.f: It is a draft animal and a milk giver. Real buffalo mozzarella is made from its milk.

yak.m: up to 1.7 m shoulder height, up to 800 kg
yak.f: Its dense fur keeps it warm down to minus 40 degrees. For people in Tibet it is transport, milk and wool in one.

lama.m: up to 1.2 m shoulder height, up to 200 kg
lama.f: A pack animal in the Andes for over 4,000 years. It spits when something does not suit it.

alpaka.m: up to 0.9 m shoulder height, up to 65 kg
alpaka.f: Bred for its fine wool, smaller than the llama.

kuh.m: up to 1.5 m shoulder height, up to 1,000 kg
kuh.f: The stomach has 4 sections, and the food is chewed again.

schaf.m: up to 0.9 m shoulder height, up to 120 kg
schaf.f: Sheep recognize each other by their faces, sometimes even after 2 years.

pferd.wo: Worldwide, origin in the steppes of Eurasia
pferd.m: up to 1.8 m shoulder height, up to 1,000 kg
pferd.f: Horses can doze while standing because they lock their legs in place.

ziege.m: up to 0.9 m shoulder height, up to 80 kg
ziege.f: One of the very first domestic animals. In Morocco, goats even climb argan trees.

schwein.m: up to 1 m shoulder height, up to 300 kg
schwein.f: Pigs are very smart and learn faster than many dogs.

esel.m: up to 1.4 m shoulder height, up to 400 kg
esel.f: Seen as stubborn, but it only checks carefully whether a path is safe.

huhn.wo: Worldwide, the most common farm animal
huhn.m: up to 0.5 m long, up to 5 kg
huhn.f: Descends from the red junglefowl of Southeast Asia, and so in a direct line from the dinosaurs.

katze.m: up to 0.5 m long, up to 6 kg
katze.f: Istanbul is famous for its free roaming cats, which are cared for by everyone.

hund.f: The oldest domestic animal, at our side for at least 15,000 years. Its nose is around 10,000 times finer than ours.

trampeltier.m: up to 2.3 m hump height, up to 1,000 kg
trampeltier.s: domestic animal, wild form critically endangered
trampeltier.f: Two humps and dense winter fur: it withstands cold of minus 40 degrees.

strauss.m: up to 2.8 m tall, up to 150 kg
strauss.f: The largest bird in the world, it runs up to 70 km/h. It does not stick its head in the sand.

emu.m: up to 1.9 m tall, up to 55 kg
emu.f: The male incubates the eggs for 8 weeks and eats almost nothing during that time.

flamingo.m: up to 1.5 m tall, up to 4 kg
flamingo.f: The pink color comes from its food. It feeds with its head upside down.

storch.m: up to 1.1 m tall, 2 m wingspan
storch.f: Flies up to 10,000 km to its winter home and uses warm rising air instead of flapping its wings.

reiher.m: up to 1 m tall, up to 2 kg
reiher.f: Stands motionless for minutes and then strikes in a flash.

pfau.m: up to 2.3 m long including train, up to 6 kg
pfau.f: The national bird of India. Only the male carries the magnificent train.

ente.m: up to 0.6 m long, up to 1.5 kg
ente.f: The wild ancestor of almost all domestic ducks.

gans.m: up to 0.9 m long, up to 4 kg
gans.f: It flies in a wedge formation. Each bird saves energy in the slipstream of the one in front.

schwan.m: up to 1.6 m long, up to 13 kg
schwan.f: One of the heaviest flying birds. Pairs usually stay together for life.

pelikan.m: up to 1.75 m long, up to 15 kg
pelikan.f: The throat pouch holds over 10 liters. Often several pelicans fish together in a half circle.

moewe.m: up to 0.65 m long, 1.5 m wingspan
moewe.f: It drops mussels from the air to crack them open.

pinguin.m: up to 0.7 m tall, up to 6 kg
pinguin.f: Builds nests from stones and sometimes steals them from its neighbor. Underwater it flies with its wings.

adler.m: up to 2.3 m wingspan, up to 6 kg
adler.f: Over 240 km/h in a dive. Its eye can spot a hare from 3 km away.

geier.m: up to 2.2 m wingspan, up to 7 kg
geier.f: Vultures are the health police of the savanna. They clear away carcasses before diseases spread.

kondor.m: over 3 m wingspan, up to 15 kg
kondor.f: One of the largest flying birds. It soars for hours almost without flapping its wings.

kraehe.m: up to 0.5 m long, 1 m wingspan
kraehe.f: Very smart: crows recognize faces and use cars to crack nuts.

ara.m: up to 0.9 m long, up to 1.2 kg
ara.f: Its beak cracks the hardest nuts. Pairs fly close next to each other.

papagei.f: Around 400 species. They hold food with their foot and can imitate voices.

taube.m: up to 0.35 m long, up to 0.4 kg
taube.f: It descends from rock doves and finds its way home over hundreds of kilometers.

kiwi.m: up to 0.5 m long, up to 3 kg
kiwi.f: It cannot fly and has its nostrils at the tip of its beak. Its egg weighs about a fifth of the female.

kasuar.m: up to 1.8 m tall, up to 70 kg
kasuar.f: It spreads the seeds of many rainforest trees. Its claws grow about 12 cm long.

uhu.m: up to 0.75 m long, 1.8 m wingspan
uhu.f: The largest owl in Europe. Thanks to soft feather edges, it flies almost silently.

tukan.m: up to 0.65 m long, up to 0.8 kg
tukan.f: The huge beak is light and also works as an air conditioner, as it gives off heat.

krokodil.m: up to 5 m long, up to 750 kg
krokodil.f: Crocodiles have existed almost unchanged for about 200 million years. The mother carries her young to the water in her mouth.

waran.m: up to 2.5 m long, up to 25 kg
waran.f: Swims excellently and lives in the middle of Bangkok in Lumphini Park.

eidechse.f: In danger it drops its tail, and it grows back.

landschildkroete.m: up to 0.25 m long, up to 3 kg
landschildkroete.f: It can live over 50 years. The shell is firmly fused with the skeleton.

schlange.r: Almost everywhere except in the cold
schlange.f: Around 4,000 species, most of them harmless. It smells with its tongue.

alligator.m: up to 4.5 m long, up to 450 kg
alligator.f: The temperature in the nest decides whether males or females hatch.

komodowaran.m: up to 3 m long, up to 90 kg
komodowaran.f: The largest lizard in the world. Its bite contains venom.

chamaeleon.f: The eyes move independently of each other. The color change serves mainly for communication.

frosch.f: An amphibian, not a reptile. It often hibernates at the bottom of ponds and then breathes through its skin.

robbe.m: up to 1.9 m long, up to 150 kg
robbe.f: Dives for up to 30 minutes and also sleeps underwater.

seeloewe.m: up to 2.4 m long, up to 390 kg
seeloewe.f: Lies on the docks at Pier 39 in San Francisco. Unlike seals, it can walk on all fours.

walross.m: up to 3.6 m long, up to 1,700 kg
walross.f: The tusks also serve as hooks to pull itself onto the ice.

delfin.m: up to 4 m long, up to 650 kg
delfin.f: Dolphins give each other their own names: every animal has a personal whistle.

orca.m: up to 9 m long, up to 6,000 kg
orca.f: The largest dolphin. Every group has its own hunting technique and passes it on.

wal.m: up to 16 m long, up to 40,000 kg
wal.f: The males sing songs that last for hours. The population has recovered since whaling.

pottwal.m: up to 18 m long, up to 57,000 kg
pottwal.f: Dives over 2,000 m deep and has the largest brain of all animals.

hai.wo: Worldwide in warm and temperate seas
hai.m: up to 3.8 m long, up to 200 kg
hai.f: Migrates over thousands of kilometers. Humans are far more dangerous to sharks than the other way around.

mantarochen.m: up to 7 m wingspan, up to 2,000 kg
mantarochen.f: Harmless despite its size. For its body size it has the largest brain of all fish.

meeresschildkroete.m: up to 1.5 m long, up to 300 kg
meeresschildkroete.f: It returns to lay eggs on the beach where it hatched itself.

thunfisch.m: up to 3 m long, up to 680 kg
thunfisch.f: One of the fastest fish, and unlike most it keeps its body warm.

fliegender_fisch.f: They glide over 100 m through the air to escape hunters.

korallenfische.f: Reefs cover under 1 percent of the sea floor and are home to about a quarter of all marine species.

hering.f: Schools of billions of animals move like a single body.

seekuh.m: up to 4 m long, up to 1,500 kg
seekuh.f: It eats about a tenth of its body weight a day. Its closest relative on land is the elephant.

krake.m: up to 1.3 m long, up to 10 kg
krake.f: It has 3 hearts and blue blood, opens screw top jars and escapes through the smallest gaps.

qualle.f: It is about 95 percent water and has neither brain nor heart.

biene.f: With the waggle dance it shows others where the food is. Many plants need bees for pollination.

schmetterling.f: The eyespots on the wings scare birds.

libelle.f: Has existed for over 300 million years. It can hover in the air and fly backwards.

motte.f: Artificial light throws them off course because they navigate by the sky.

gluehwuermchen.f: Not a worm, but a beetle. Its cold light is produced almost without losing heat.
